title: Quiche Lorraine with Mustard Potato Salad
basedOn: RecipeTin Eats — Quiche Lorraine — Nagi Maehashi

ingredients.swap: Keep the spring onions in a small bowl and stir them into one portion of potato salad only.

steps.title: Get prepped
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan and put a baking tray in to heat. Take the pastry out of the fridge 10 min before unrolling so it doesn't crack. Finely chop the onion, crush the garlic and cut the bacon into thin strips. Grate the cheddar.

steps.title: Line the tin
steps.text: Unroll the pastry and press it into a 20cm loose-bottomed tart tin, letting the excess hang over the edge. Prick the base all over with a fork. Line with scrunched-up baking paper and fill with baking beans or uncooked rice.

steps.title: Blind-bake the case
steps.text: Bake on the hot tray for 15 min until the edges are set. Lift out the paper and beans, then bake for 8–10 min more until the base looks dry and pale golden. Trim the overhanging pastry with a sharp knife.

steps.title: Fry the bacon
steps.text: While the case bakes, melt the butter in a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the bacon, onion and garlic for 6–8 min until the bacon is light golden and the onion is soft. Tip onto kitchen paper to drain and cool a little.

steps.title: Fill and bake the quiche
steps.text: Whisk the eggs and cream in a jug with a good grind of black pepper; the bacon brings enough salt. Scatter the bacon mixture over the pastry case, then the cheddar. Pour in the egg mix and push some filling under the surface. Bake for 30–35 min until golden on top with a slight wobble in the centre.

steps.title: Cook the potatoes
steps.text: Once the quiche is in the oven, put the potatoes in a saucepan of cold salted water. Bring to the boil and simmer for 12–15 min until a knife slides in easily. Drain and leave to steam-dry for 10 min.

steps.title: Dress the potato salad
steps.text: In a large bowl, mix the mayo, mustard and lemon juice with a pinch of salt and pepper. Fold in the warm potatoes, then scatter over the spring onions.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Leave the quiche in its tin for 10 min so it sets and slices cleanly. Cut into 4 and serve 2 slices each with the potato salad and little gem leaves (optional).

photo.alt: A golden baked quiche in a cast-iron skillet

title: Pork & Apple Burgers with Cheddar & Crunchy Slaw
basedOn: Tesco Real Food — Pork and apple burgers — Tesco Real Food team

ingredients.t: 1, half grated and half cut into matchsticks

steps.title: Prep the veg
steps.text: Heat the grill to medium-high and line the grill pan with foil. Peel and coarsely grate the carrot. Grate half the apple, skin on, and cut the other half into thin matchsticks. Finely shred the red cabbage.

steps.title: Shape the burgers
steps.text: In a bowl, mix the pork mince, grated apple, half the carrot, the panko, Worcestershire sauce and egg with a pinch of salt and pepper. With damp hands, shape into 2 patties about 2cm thick and a little wider than the buns. Press a shallow dip in the middle of each so they stay flat. Chill for 10 min.

steps.title: Make the slaw and sauce
steps.text: While the burgers chill, mix half the mayo with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Toss in the red cabbage, apple matchsticks and remaining carrot. In a small bowl, stir the rest of the mayo with the mustard for the burgers.

steps.title: Grill the burgers
steps.text: Brush the patties with the oil and grill for 7–8 min on each side until golden. They're ready when there's no pink in the middle and the juices run clear.

steps.title: Melt the cheese
steps.text: Lay the cheddar over the burgers and grill for 1 min until melted. Move them to a plate to rest. Toast the cut sides of the buns under the grill for 30–60 sec, watching closely.

steps.title: Build and serve
steps.text: Spread the mustard mayo over the bun bases and add the little gem. Top with the cheesy burgers and the lids. Serve with the slaw on the side.

photo.alt: A burger with lettuce and tomato in a toasted bun

title: Sticky BBQ Ribs with Paprika Wedges & Slaw
basedOn: RecipeTin Eats — Oven Pork Ribs with Barbecue Sauce — Nagi Maehashi

ingredients.swap: Scatter the spring onion over one plate only.

steps.title: Rub the ribs
steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan. Mix 2 tsp of the smoked paprika with the herbs, chilli powder (optional), 1 tsp salt and a good grind of pepper. Pat the ribs dry and rub the mix all over, mostly on the meaty side.

steps.title: Slow-bake under foil
steps.text: Lay the ribs meaty-side up in a roasting tin and pour 100ml water around them. Cover tightly with foil, sealing the edges. Bake for 1 hr 30 min until the meat is tender and starting to pull back from the bones.

steps.title: Mix the glaze
steps.text: While the ribs bake, stir the BBQ sauce, honey, Worcestershire sauce and crushed garlic together in a small bowl. Set aside until the ribs come out.

steps.title: Prep the wedges
steps.text: About 15 min before the ribs are ready, cut the potatoes into chunky wedges, skin on. Toss on a large baking tray with the oil, the remaining ½ tsp paprika and a pinch of salt. Spread out in a single layer.

steps.title: Crisp the ribs, roast the wedges
steps.text: Take the ribs out and turn the oven up to 200°C fan. Move the ribs to a foil-lined baking tray and pour away the juices. Put the ribs on the top shelf for 10 min until the rub looks crusty. Put the wedges in below and roast for 35–40 min, turning halfway, until golden.

steps.title: Glaze the ribs
steps.text: Turn the ribs bony-side up, brush with a third of the glaze and roast for 10 min. Flip, brush with half the remaining glaze and roast for 10 min more. Brush on the last of the glaze and roast for 5 min until sticky and dark at the edges.

steps.title: Make the slaw
steps.text: While the ribs glaze, mix the mayo and lemon juice with a pinch of salt in a bowl. Toss in the red cabbage and grated carrot.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Rest the ribs for 5 min, then cut between the bones. Serve with the wedges and slaw, scattered with spring onion (optional).

photo.alt: Roasted barbecue pork ribs with potatoes

title: Loaded Potato Skins with Bacon, Cheddar & Soured Cream
airFryer: After microwaving and scooping, air-fry the oiled skins at 200°C for 8–10 min until crisp, then fill and air-fry for 3–4 min until the cheese melts.
basedOn: The Mom 100 — Loaded Baked Potato Skins — Katie Workman

ingredients.swap: Scatter the spring onions over one plate of skins only.

steps.title: Get prepped
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Scrub the potatoes and prick them all over with a fork. Grate the cheddar, slice the spring onions, chop the little gem and halve the tomatoes.

steps.title: Microwave the potatoes
steps.text: Microwave the potatoes on high for 12–15 min, turning halfway, until a knife slides in easily. Leave to cool for 5 min so you can handle them.

steps.title: Fry the bacon
steps.text: While the potatoes cook, fry the bacon in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 5–6 min, turning, until crisp. Drain on kitchen paper, then chop into small pieces.

steps.title: Scoop out the skins
steps.text: Halve the potatoes lengthways. Scoop out most of the flesh with a spoon, leaving a 5mm layer inside each skin. Chill the scooped potato to use for mash or fishcakes within 2 days.

steps.title: Crisp the skins
steps.text: Brush the skins inside and out with 1 tbsp of the oil. Season with salt, pepper and the paprika (optional). Bake cut-side up on a baking tray for 15–20 min until crisp and golden at the edges.

steps.title: Load them up
steps.text: Fill the skins with the bacon and pile the cheddar on top. Bake for 5–8 min more until the cheese is melted and bubbling.

steps.title: Dress the salad and serve
steps.text: Toss the little gem and tomatoes with the remaining oil and a pinch of salt. Top each skin with a spoonful of soured cream and the spring onions (optional). Serve 3 halves each with the salad.

title: Cheesy Tuna Melts with Sweetcorn & Crunchy Salad
basedOn: MSC (Marine Stewardship Council) UK — Tuna melt

ingredients.swap: Stir the sweetcorn into half the tuna mix only, or leave it out and add a little more red onion.
Scatter the jalapeños over one person's melts only, before the cheese goes on.

steps.title: Get prepped
steps.text: Heat the grill to high. Put the sweetcorn in a sieve and pour over a kettle of boiling water to defrost it, then drain well. Finely chop the red onion and grate the cheddar. Chop the little gem, slice the cucumber and halve the tomatoes.

steps.title: Make the tuna mayo
steps.text: Drain the tuna well, pressing out the water with a fork. Mix with the mayo, red onion, sweetcorn and a good grind of black pepper. Stir in the jalapeños (optional).

steps.title: Toast the bread
steps.text: Lay the bread on a baking tray and grill for 1–2 min until golden. Turn over, thinly butter the untoasted side and grill for 1 min more.

steps.title: Grill the melts
steps.text: Spread the tuna mix over the buttered side, right to the edges. Pile the cheddar on top. Grill for 3–4 min until the cheese is bubbling and golden in patches.

steps.title: Dress the salad and serve
steps.text: While the melts grill, toss the little gem, cucumber and tomatoes with the oil and a pinch of salt. Cut the melts in half and serve 2 slices each with the salad.

title: Spicy Bean Burgers with Smashed Avocado & Wedges
airFryer: Air-fry the oiled sweet potato wedges at 200°C for 15–18 min, shaking halfway.

ingredients.swap: Stir the coriander into half the smashed avocado only.

steps.title: Get prepped
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Cut the sweet potato into wedges, skin on. Drain and rinse the beans, then pat them dry on kitchen paper. Slice the spring onions and crush the garlic.

steps.title: Roast the wedges
steps.text: Toss the wedges on a baking tray with 1 tbsp of the oil and a pinch of salt. Roast for 25–30 min, turning halfway, until tender and caramelised at the edges.

steps.title: Make the patties
steps.text: While the wedges roast, mash the beans in a bowl with a fork, leaving some chunky. Mix in the panko, egg, garlic, spring onions, chilli powder, paprika, cumin (optional) and a pinch of salt. With damp hands, shape into 2 patties about 2cm thick. Chill for 10 min to firm up.

steps.title: Smash the avocado
steps.text: Halve, stone and scoop the avocado into a bowl. Mash with the lime juice and a pinch of salt, then stir in the coriander (optional).

steps.title: Fry the burgers
steps.text: Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Fry the patties for 4–5 min on each side until crisp and hot through, turning carefully with a fish slice. Lay the cheddar on top for the last 2 min and cover the pan to melt it.

steps.title: Toast the buns
steps.text: Lift the burgers onto a plate. Wipe out the pan and toast the buns cut-side down over a medium heat for 1 min until golden.

steps.title: Build and serve
steps.text: Spread the yogurt over the bun bases and add the little gem. Top with the burgers, a spoonful of smashed avocado and the lids. Serve with the wedges.

title: Sticky Prawn & Pak Choi Noodle Stir-Fry
basedOn: Tesco Real Food — One-pot prawn and noodle stir-fry — Tesco Real Food team

ingredients.t: 3, sliced, whites and greens kept apart
ingredients.swap: Stir-fry the whites with the veg, but scatter the greens over one bowl only.
Drizzle the hot sauce over one bowl only.

ingredients.t: ½, cut into wedges, to serve

steps.title: Get prepped
steps.text: Put the kettle on. Sit the frozen prawns in a bowl of cold water for 10 min to defrost, then drain and pat dry. Slice the pepper and garlic, quarter the pak choi and slice the spring onions, keeping whites and greens apart. Mix the soy, oyster and sweet chilli sauces in a small bowl.

steps.title: Cook the noodles
steps.text: Cook the noodles in a saucepan of boiling water for 4 min, or as the packet says, until just tender. Drain, rinse under cold water and toss with 1 tsp of the oil so they don't stick.

steps.title: Fry the prawns
steps.text: Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in a wok or large frying pan over a high heat. Stir-fry the prawns for 2–3 min until pink all over. Tip onto a plate.

steps.title: Stir-fry the veg
steps.text: Add the pepper, garlic, ginger and spring onion whites to the wok and stir-fry for 2 min. Add the pak choi and cook for 2 min more until the leaves wilt but the stalks stay crisp.

steps.title: Toss it all together
steps.text: Return the prawns to the wok with the noodles and sauce. Toss over a high heat for 1–2 min until the noodles are glossy and piping hot. Stir in the hot sauce (optional) and sesame oil (optional).

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pile into bowls and scatter over the spring onion greens. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing (optional).

title: Singapore Noodles with Prawns & Sticky Pork
basedOn: RecipeTin Eats — Singapore Noodles — Nagi Maehashi

ingredients.swap: Stir-fry the beansprouts in a separate pan for 1 min and add to one portion only.
Scatter the spring onions over one portion only.
Scatter the chilli over one portion only.

steps.title: Get prepped
steps.text: Put the kettle on. Sit the frozen prawns in a bowl of cold water for 10 min to defrost, then drain and pat dry. Slice the onion and pepper and crush the garlic. In a small bowl, mix the soy sauce, curry powder, honey, black pepper and 2 tbsp water.

steps.title: Soak the noodles
steps.text: Put the noodles in a heatproof bowl and cover with just-boiled water. Soak for 6–8 min, or as the packet says, until soft but not mushy. Drain, rinse under cold water and drain well again.

steps.title: Cook the pork
steps.text: Brush the pork all over with the hoisin. Heat 1 tsp of the oil in a wok or large frying pan over a medium heat. Fry the pork for 3–4 min on each side until sticky, caramelised and cooked through with no pink. Rest on a board, then slice thinly.

steps.title: Cook the prawns
steps.text: Wipe out the wok and heat another 1 tsp oil over a medium heat. Cook the prawns for 2–3 min, turning, until pink all over. Tip onto a plate.

steps.title: Make the omelette
steps.text: Add 1 tsp oil to the wok, pour in the eggs and swirl into a thin omelette. Cook for 1 min until set, then roll it up, slide it onto a board and slice into ribbons.

steps.title: Fry the veg
steps.text: Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in the wok over a medium-high heat. Stir-fry the onion, garlic and ginger for 2 min until softened. Add the pepper and cook for 1 min more.

steps.title: Toss and serve
steps.text: Add the noodles and sauce and toss with tongs until evenly yellow. Add the pork, prawns, egg and beansprouts (optional) and toss for 1–2 min until hot through. Serve topped with the spring onions and chilli (optional).

title: Crispy Chinese Lemon Chicken with Rice & Broccoli
basedOn: RecipeTin Eats — Crispy Chinese Lemon Chicken — Nagi Maehashi

ingredients.swap: Scatter the spring onion over one plate only.

steps.title: Get prepped
steps.text: Put the kettle on. Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally to make 4 thin steaks, then season with ½ tsp salt. For the batter, whisk 30g cornflour, the flour and a pinch of salt in a bowl and chill. Spread 20g cornflour on a plate. Dissolve the stock cube in 100ml boiling water, juice 2 lemons and slice the rest.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice and put it in a saucepan with 300ml boiling water and a pinch of salt. Bring back to the boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 min. Take off the heat and leave covered for 5 min.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Pour the oil into a deep, heavy saucepan or wok to about 4cm deep, no more than a third full. Heat over a medium-high heat to 160°C, when a cube of bread turns golden in about 40 sec. Never leave hot oil unattended.

steps.title: Give the chicken a first fry
steps.text: Coat the chicken in the plate of cornflour and shake off the excess. Whisk 90ml ice-cold water into the batter until just combined; small lumps are fine. Dip each piece, let the excess drip off and fry 2 at a time for 3 min until pale golden. Drain on kitchen paper and leave to rest for 10 min.

steps.title: Make the lemon sauce
steps.text: While the chicken rests, mix the remaining 10g cornflour with a splash of the stock in a small saucepan until smooth. Stir in the rest of the stock, the lemon juice, honey, garlic and ginger. Simmer over a medium heat, stirring, for 2–3 min until glossy and the consistency of runny honey. Keep warm on the lowest heat.

steps.title: Cook the broccoli
steps.text: Cook the broccoli in a pan of boiling salted water for 3–4 min until just tender. Drain and keep warm in the pan.

steps.title: Give the chicken a second fry
steps.text: Turn the oil up to 190°C, when a cube of bread browns in about 15 sec. Fry the chicken 2 pieces at a time for 2–3 min, turning halfway, until deep golden, crisp and cooked through with no pink. Drain on kitchen paper.

steps.title: Slice and serve
steps.text: Slice the chicken into 2cm strips and lay over the rice with the broccoli alongside. Spoon over the lemon sauce and top with lemon slices and spring onion (optional). Let the oil cool completely, then strain it to reuse or bin it; never pour it down the sink.
